content: Buspirone is a medication prescribed to treat anxiety disorders or to manage symptoms of anxiety in the short term. It may also be prescribed for other uses, so consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Buspirone is available in tablet form and is taken orally, typically two or three times a day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take buspirone exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of it or take it more frequently than prescribed. Continue taking buspirone even if you feel well. Do not stop taking it without consulting your doctor, especially if you have been on high doses for an extended period. Your doctor may gradually reduce your dose to prevent withdrawal symptoms. It may take several weeks of regular use before the full effects of the medication are felt. Buspirone is sometimes used to treat symptoms of premenstrual syndrome (PMS). Discuss the potential risks of using this medication for your condition with your doctor. Before taking buspirone, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to buspirone or any other medications. Also, disclose all other medications you are taking, including prescription and over-the-counter drugs, vitamins, and supplements, particularly erythromycin, haloperidol, ketoconazole, itraconazole, MAO inhibitors, muscle relaxants, nefazodone, pain medications or narcotics, rifampin, ritonavir, sedatives, sleeping pills, tranquilizers, trazodone, verapamil, and others. Let your doctor know if you have or have ever had kidney or liver disease or a history of alcohol or drug abuse. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking buspirone, contact your doctor immediately. If you are undergoing surgery, including dental surgery, inform your doctor or dentist that you are taking buspirone. Be aware that this medication may cause drowsiness. Avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you. Alcohol can increase the drowsiness caused by this medication, so avoid consuming alcohol while taking buspirone. You can take buspirone with or without food, but it is important to be consistent—always take it either with food or without food. Avoid consuming large amounts of grapefruit juice while taking this medication. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is within four hours of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Buspirone may cause side effects. Inform your doctor if any of the following symptoms are severe or persistent: drowsiness, upset stomach, vomiting, constipation, diarrhea, stomach pain, headache, dry mouth, depression, excitement, fatigue, nervousness, difficulty sleeping, lightheadedness, weakness, or numbness. If you experience any of the following severe side effects, contact your doctor immediately: skin rash, itching, fast or irregular heartbeat, blurred vision, or unusual movements of the head or neck muscles. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store buspirone in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from light, excess heat, and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of outdated or no longer needed medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call 911. Symptoms of overdose may include upset stomach, vomiting, dizziness, drowsiness, and blurred vision. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Your doctor may order lab tests to monitor your response to buspirone. Do not share your medication with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription.
